marks.gloss_en: R' Abba: Ahasuerus and Haman are like two men, one with a mound in his field and one with a ditch in his field
the ditch-owner said: sell me your mound! he said: take it for free, and gladly! -- ['the silver is given to you, and the people', Esth 3:11]
R' Abba bar Kahana: the removal of the ring was greater than the forty-eight prophets and seven prophetesses -- they did not bring Israel back to good, while the removal of the ring did

ומה מעבדות לחירות אמרינן שירה -- ממיתה לחיים לא כל שכן: if song is said for slavery-to-freedom, then for death-to-life all the more (= p_kv_mimita_lechayim, how the prophets derived the reading of the Megilla)
what did they expound? R' Chiya bar Avin in R' Yehoshua ben Korcha's name: if from slavery to freedom we say song, from death to life all the more so
כדתניא: עד שלא נכנסו ישראל לארץ הוכשרו כל ארצות לומר שירה -- why the Exodus is not a counterexample
כדתניא: עד שלא נכנסו ישראל לארץ הוכשרו כל ארצות לומר שירה (= p_huchsheru_kol_haaratzot)
a baraita: until Israel entered the Land all lands were fit for saying song [over their miracles]; once Israel entered the Land, the other lands were no longer fit
כדתניא: הרבה נביאים עמדו להם לישראל, כפלים כיוצאי מצרים
מיהוה טובא הוו ... נבואה שהוצרכה לדורות נכתבה (= p_nevua_letzorech_dorot)
there were indeed many, but prophecy needed for the generations was written and that not needed was not written
אי הכי, הלל נמי נימא! -- if the kal vachomer obliges song, let Hallel be said on Purim too
לפי שאין אומרים הלל על נס שבחוצה לארץ (= p_ein_hallel_chutz)
יציאת מצרים, דנס שבחוצה לארץ, היכי אמרינן שירה? -- the Exodus was a miracle outside the Land, yet song is said for it
[the stam answers:] because Hallel is not said over a miracle outside the Land
קריייתה זו הלילה (= p_kriata_hallela)
אכתי עבדי אחשורוש אנן (= p_akati_avdei_achashverosh)
Rav Nachman: its reading [of the Megilla] is its Hallel
בין לרבא בין לרב נחמן קשיא, והא תניא: משנכנסו לארץ לא הוכשרו כל הארצות לומר שירה -- Rav Nachman's answer presumes Hallel would otherwise be due for a miracle outside the Land
כיון שגלו, חזרו להכשירן הראשון (= p_kevan_shegalu)
בין לרבא בין לרב נחמן קשיא -- the same baraita against Rava's answer
כיון שגלו, חזרו להכשירן הראשון (= p_kevan_shegalu)
once they were exiled, [the lands] returned to their original fitness
ותו ליכא? והכתיב: ויהי איש אחד מן הרמתים צופים -- אחד ממאתים צופים -- were there no more than forty-eight?
but it is written 'there was a man from Ramatayim-Tzofim' (1 Sam 1:1) -- one of two hundred seers who prophesied to Israel
the Rabbis taught: forty-eight prophets and seven prophetesses prophesied to Israel and neither subtracted from nor added to what is written in the Torah, except for the reading of the Megilla
R' Shmuel bar Nachmani: a man who came from two heights that face each other
בסתר ההר? מן ההר מיבעי ליה! -- 'from the mountain' would be expected
Avigail, as written 'she was riding on the donkey and coming down in the covert of the mountain' (1 Sam 25:20) -- object of the difficulty
על עסקי דם הבא מן הסתרים (= p_dam_min_hastarim)
Rabba bar Shmuel: concerning blood that comes from the hidden parts
who are the seven prophetesses? Sarah, Miriam, Devorah, Chana, Avigail, Chulda and Esther

Miriam, as written 'Miriam the prophetess, sister of Aaron' (Ex 15:20) and not of Moses: Rav Nachman in Rav's name -- she prophesied while she was [only] Aaron's sister: my mother is destined to bear a son who will save Israel
when they cast him into the river, her father tapped her head: my daughter, where is your prophecy?
Devorah, as written 'Devorah, a prophetess, wife of Lapidot' (Judg 4:4): what is 'wife of Lapidot'? she made wicks for the Sanctuary
'she sat under the palm' (Judg 4:5) -- why under a palm? R' Shimon ben Avshalom: because of [avoiding] seclusion

Chana, as written 'my horn is exalted in the Lord' (1 Sam 2:1): 'my horn', not 'my flask' -- David and Solomon, anointed from a horn, their kingship lasted; Saul and Jehu, anointed from a flask, did not

'there is none holy like the Lord, for there is none besides You (biltecha)' (1 Sam 2:2): Rav Yehuda bar Menashya -- read 'to outlast You (levalotecha)': a man's works outlast him, but the Holy One outlasts His works
'and there is no rock (tzur) like our God' -- no artist (tzayar) like our God: a man paints a form on a wall and cannot put breath and soul in it; the Holy One forms a form within a form
